solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One responsible for moving scenes observed in theatre?

definitions.text: One responsible for moving scenes observed in theatre?

parts.words: One responsible for moving scenes observed in theatre
parts.note: the moving of scenes sounds emotional, but it is a backstage worker shifting scenery that the audience watches

explanation.surface: Someone whose job is to make audiences weep at affecting moments in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre worker who shifts the scenery between acts is exactly one who moves scenes.

clue.text: Small branches ultimately first and second to stock syrup

indicators.note: to stock means to hold within, so the outer letters keep the wig inside them
ultimately points to the final letter of the word first

parts.note: syrup is rhyming slang for wig, from syrup of figs

explanation.surface: Little bits of a tree ending up in a jar of syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Syrup' is Cockney rhyming slang: syrup of figs rhymes with wig.
explanation.definitionFit: Twigs are the thin, small shoots growing off a tree's larger limbs.

clue.text: Looked angrily about — happy to be taken outside

indicators.note: the happy word goes round the outside of the about word, enclosing it

parts.note: happy means glad
re is a short word meaning about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone scowled around, glad to be marched out of the room.
explanation.definitionFit: To glare is to stare with fury, so the past tense means looked angrily.

clue.text: German individual stops sheep scratching at soil

indicators.note: stops here means plugs, the German word sitting inside the sheep word like a stopper

parts.note: a hog or hogg is a young sheep not yet shorn
ein is German for one, a single individual

explanation.surface: A lone German blocks a flock of sheep that are pawing at the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: HOG as a sheep is a farming term for a yearling before its first shearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Working the ground with a hoe is breaking up the surface earth, a kind of scratching.

clue.text: Martial artist from South filled with excellent spirit in spring

indicators.note: filled with means the reversed word has the excellent letters put inside it
in a down answer, reading from the south means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: a dan is a graded expert in judo or karate
A1 means first-rate, written AI

explanation.surface: A fighter from the south is overflowing with fine spirit come springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season; it is a water source, home of a water nymph.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a water nymph inhabited a river, fountain or spring.

clue.text: Celebrate host dancing for girls in New York?

indicators.note: dancing letters jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: Throw a party and dance, ideal for a night out of girls in Manhattan.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: the term is American, so the girls are placed in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: This American term names unmarried young women, especially those on a hen night.

clue.text: Ragged person in Comedy Store?

definitions.meaning: ragged means teased or mocked, so this is someone made a figure of fun
read playfully, a store or stock of laughter; the Comedy Store is also a London comedy club

explanation.surface: A scruffy figure turns up at a comedy club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ragged' looks like tattered clothes but is the British verb rag, to tease.
explanation.definitionFit: A person everyone mocks is the butt of jokes, and a supply of laughs is a stock of them.

clue.text: Certain animal — cuckoo from Brazil?

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so the letters go mad and rearrange

explanation.surface: A particular creature, a cuckoo, hails from Brazil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuckoo' looks like the bird the animal is; it is the anagram signal. The question mark shows the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazil is in the southern Americas, so a Brazilian is an example of someone from that region.

clue.text: Count up notes and visit official receiver?

parts.note: to count up is to add
re is a note of the sol-fa scale, so res are notes
to see someone is to visit them

explanation.surface: A bankruptcy official tots up banknotes and calls round.
explanation.walkthrough: An official receiver in Britain manages bankruptcies; here it is one who officially receives a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The named recipient of a letter or parcel is its formal receiver.

clue.text: Carried on working unnoticed

indicators.note: working suggests letters in motion, being reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone kept on toiling with nobody noticing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' looks like part of the definition but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going without stopping is to persist or proceed further.

clue.text: Bill sent back hot and oddly lush Indian food

indicators.note: sent back means the bill word is read in reverse

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a bill or poster
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: oddly takes the first and third letters of lush

explanation.surface: The bill for a hot, rather lavish curry is returned.
explanation.definitionFit: Dhal or dal is a lentil dish from South Asian cuisine, here as a plural.

clue.text: Remaining quietly hidden takes trouble and effort

parts.note: to dog someone is to trouble or plague them
a go is an attempt or effort

explanation.surface: Keeping a low profile takes a lot of hassle and work.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is British slang, used in the phrase 'lie doggo'.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie doggo is to stay still and out of sight, keeping low.

clue.text: Saw an American lawyer for example rebuffed

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney in the US

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so the example letters run backwards

explanation.surface: I saw a US attorney get turned down, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a verb; it is the noun meaning an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old proverb or maxim, a traditional saying.

clue.text: Bewildered? Worse things can happen here!

definitions.meaning: the proverb says worse things happen on the ocean, to console after a mishap

explanation.surface: Puzzled? Cheer up, it could be worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lost on the ocean is an idiom for confusion, and the proverb places worse fates on the ocean.

clue.text: American to regret curtailed affair

indicators.note: curtailed means its tail, the last letter, is cut off

parts.note: to mourn is to grieve or regret

explanation.surface: A US citizen comes to rue a love affair cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: This French borrowing means a love affair, often a secret one.

clue.text: John might follow this student in exclusive institution

indicators.note: in means the student letter is placed inside the school

parts.note: Eton is an exclusive English private school
L stands for learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A pupil named John might well be one at a posh school.
explanation.walkthrough: John is the singer Elton John, so the answer comes before his surname. ETON is Britain's most famous private boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: The pop star's full stage name puts his first name before the word John.

clue.text: Moderate happening not long ago to change party

indicators.note: changing party here swaps the Conservative letter for the Liberal one

parts.note: recent means happening lately

explanation.surface: A centrist who recently defected to another party.
explanation.walkthrough: C (Conservative) is swapped for L (Liberal), British party abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: To relent is to soften or ease up, to become less severe.

clue.text: Officer having penned song becomes stockholder?

indicators.note: having penned means enclosing, the officer letters fencing in the song

parts.note: Lt abbreviates lieutenant, an officer
an aria is a song in opera

explanation.surface: A singing officer turns shareholder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stockholder' looks financial; it is one who holds livestock with a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope with a running noose is used by cowboys to catch and hold cattle.

clue.text: Dwarf rudely abrupt

definitions.meaning: as an adjective, dwarf means small or stunted in height

explanation.surface: A little man who is curt and rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Small of stature and curt of speech are both senses of the same common adjective.

clue.text: Struggle when river invades Cornish town endlessly

indicators.note: invades means the river letter pushes into the town
endlessly means losing the final letter

parts.note: St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A seaside town in Cornwall battles a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: ST IVES is a resort in Cornwall, England's south-western tip.
explanation.definitionFit: To strive is to make great efforts, to fight hard.

clue.text: Gore moved ahead in Portland region

indicators.note: moved means the letters are shifted around

parts.note: on means ahead or forward, as in move on

explanation.surface: Al Gore pulled ahead in a district around Portland.
explanation.definitionFit: The city of Portland lies in this Pacific Northwest US state.

clue.text: Item with Oedipal strings attached?

parts.note: an Oedipal attachment is a son clinging to his mother, and the kitchen garment she wears has ties that he stays tied to

explanation.surface: A relationship with an unhealthy maternal bond.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom is being tied to your mother's apron strings, too dependent on her; Oedipal makes the mother link.
explanation.definitionFit: This kitchen garment has ties, and a man tied to his mother's ties is too dependent on her.

clue.text: Stuff one has to leave in place

indicators.note: in means one plus leave go inside the place word

parts.note: to put is to place
I is the Roman numeral one
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: Things someone must leave behind where they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a noun but is the verb, to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff oneself is to gorge, eat to excess.

clue.text: Haunt of drunken bosses

indicators.note: drunken letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: A pub frequented by tipsy managers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haunt' looks like a noun, a favourite spot; it is the verb, to preoccupy.
explanation.definitionFit: To haunt someone's mind is to preoccupy them constantly.

clue.text: Run to leave tenant key

indicators.note: to leave means the run letter goes from the tenant word

parts.note: a renter is one who rents, a tenant
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A lodger told to quit is handed a door key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' is a computer keyboard key, not a door key.
explanation.definitionFit: The return button on a keyboard is labelled with this word.

clue.text: Aussie bouncers? Opener in terror bats here!

parts.note: roos are kangaroos, Australia's bouncing animals

indicators.note: the opener in a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Australian nightclub doormen terrified by an opening batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncers' and 'bats' suggest cricket; they are kangaroos and the flying mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: Bats, like birds, gather to rest in a perch or sleeping place.

clue.text: Device ultimately used to finish wooden strip?

definitions.text: Device ultimately used to finish wooden strip?

indicators.note: to finish means that letter goes at the end, after the strip

parts.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word device

explanation.surface: A tool is finally used to finish off a wooden batten.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue also describes a woodturner's tool that shapes and finishes a piece of wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodturner's machine that spins work against a cutting tool.

clue.text: Will takes canoe at last into Wash

indicators.note: into means that letter goes inside the wash word

parts.note: to lave is an old word for to wash

indicators.note: at last picks out the final letter of canoe

explanation.surface: Will puts a canoe into the Wash, an East Anglian bay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like a name; it is the verb, to bequeath. The Wash is a bay on England's east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To will property is to bequeath it, to pass it on at death.

clue.text: Uncompromising approach in 'Enduring Love'?

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring
enduring something is tolerating it, showing tolerance

explanation.surface: A hardline stance in a novel called Enduring Love.
explanation.walkthrough: Enduring Love is a novel by Ian McEwan. Read the other way, the answer is tolerance of nil, i.e. enduring love.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy of no leniency at all for any offence is a strict, unbending approach.

clue.text: Politicians say involving me in partnership

parts.note: to state is to say

indicators.note: involving means the partnership letters enclose me

parts.note: in bridge, South and North are a partnership

explanation.surface: Politicians claim they include me in a coalition.
explanation.walkthrough: N and S are the North-South pair in bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Statesmen are experienced and respected political leaders.
